beats.beat: The company sells four categories of specialty chemicals: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM) and Hard Minerals (HM). These are used across diverse industries.
It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's network. This is a key dependency.
Customer concentration is high: the top 10 customers accounted for roughly 59% of revenue from operations in each of the last three fiscal years (FY2015, FY2016, FY2017).
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka, with total exports of ₹1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.

beats.beat: The promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and corporate entity 20 Microns Limited.
Promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity share capital. The promoter group (excluding promoters) holds only 0.24% (21,510 shares).

The authorises share capital is ₹2,000 lakh (20,00,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each) and the issued, subscribed and paid-up capital is ₹897 lakh (89,70,000 equity shares of ₹10 each) as at September 30, 2017.
Related party transactions have occurred over the last five financial years and the six months ended September 30, 2017, as per Accounting Standard 18. The DRHP cross-references page 223 for details.
The company, its promoters, group companies and directors are parties to certain legal proceedings – any adverse outcome could materially affect business.

There have been instances of non-filing or incorrect or delayed filings with the Registrar of Companies, and the company has not yet obtained all statutory licenses for one of its manufacturing facilities (Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia).

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals segment (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at ₹1,443 billion in fiscal 2017, having grown at 10-12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017. CRISIL Research forecasts 12-14% CAGR going forward.
The industry is highly fragmented: small and medium enterprises hold 70-75% market share. Only a few Indian players have the scale to compete with global giants on product development.

Growth drivers include rising middle-class consumption, urbanisation, 100% FDI allowance in chemicals, and a Draft National Chemical Policy aimed at increasing the sector's GDP share. Import substitution is a stated opportunity — India's chemicals imports (6.4% CAGR) have outpaced exports (6% CAGR).
Sub-segments like construction chemicals, water chemicals and personal care ingredients are each expected to grow at 15% CAGR over the next three to five years.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals — mainly functional additives and chemically modified minerals — and relies on a long-term marketing arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited.

The company is raising capital through a fresh issue of equity shares on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE), managed by Vivro Financial Services Private Limited. Proceeds will fund a new manufacturing facility at GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and other corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares (no offer for sale). The specific number of shares and price band are not disclosed in the DRHP excerpts.

Proceeds will be used to (1) fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; (2) general corporate purposes; and (3) create a public trading market for equity shares by listing on NSE EMERGE, enhancing visibility and brand.
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited; the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

beats.beat: No long-term agreements with customers or raw material suppliers. The company operates on purchase orders, exposing it to volume, pricing and supply volatility.
Negative cash flows from operations occurred in the past (e.g., ₹349.75 lakh outflow in FY2014). Sustained negative cash flow could impair growth and operations.

The company lacks certain statutory licenses and registrations required for one of its manufacturing facilities (Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia). Non-compliance could lead to penalties or operational disruptions.
Promoters control 99.76% of pre-issue equity and related party transactions are material. This creates potential for conflicts of interest and limits minority shareholder influence.
The company, its promoters and group entities are involved in legal proceedings. An adverse outcome could materially affect financial condition and reputation.
